en: Title: *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* Edited by: Leumann (1912), Izumi & Togano (1917) [Source of Input] Source: This is the Khotanese bilingual fragment without the Khotanese text.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lady Prajñāpāramitā! Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was [with] the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
And with Ākāśagarbha,
and Vajramuṣṭi,
and Mañjuśrī.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, who turns the wheel of Dharma upon the arising of the thought of awakening; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamārapramardin.

With these eight koṭis of bodhisattvas as their leaders, he taught me—[whose name is missing]—a teaching that is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end; excellent in meaning, well-phrased in syllables, unconfused, pure, and the extraction of the purification of the method of all dharmas.
This is the stage of the purity of the good mind, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of purity of view, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva. This is the stage of purity of delight, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of purity of craving, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of purity of adornment, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of purity of delight, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of purity of light, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of purity of bodily bliss, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of purity of speech, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the state of purity of mind, namely, the state of a bodhisattva; this is the state of purity of sound, namely, the state of a bodhisattva;
this is the state of purity of fragrance, namely, the state of a bodhisattva.
This is the stage of the purification of taste, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of the purification of touch, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
For what reason? Because all phenomena are pure by their very nature; through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, there is the purification of the perfection of wisdom.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom, which is the accomplishment of the perfect awakening to the peaceful reality-nature of all Tathāgatas: Great Awakening is the awakening to the equality of the vajra, by virtue of its adamantine firmness;
Great Awakening is the awakening to the equality of meaning, by virtue of its single purpose;
Great Awakening is the awakening to the equality of phenomena, by virtue of the purity of their intrinsic nature.
"Great awakening (*mahābodhi*) consists in the realization of the equality of all things through the non-conceptualization of everything; thus, *Aṃ*.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the subduer of all malevolent ones, again taught the extraction of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā-nirhāra*) called "The Compendium of Victory through the Equality of All Dharmas":
"Through the non-proliferation (*aprapañca*) of passion, there is the non-proliferation of hatred."

Through the non-proliferation of hatred, there is the non-proliferation of delusion; through the non-proliferation of delusion, there is the non-proliferation of all phenomena; through the non-proliferation of all phenomena, it should be known that there is the non-proliferation of the perfection of wisdom. HŪṂ.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Svabhāvaśuddha, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called the Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara who Contemplates the Equality of All Phenomena:
"The purification of all passion in the world leads to the purification of hatred;
the purification of all impurities in the world leads to the purification of all evil."
The purity of all phenomena in the world leads to the purity of all sentient beings;
the purity of all-knowledge in the world leads to the purity of the perfection of wisdom. *Hrīḥ*.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who holds the fist of all Tathāgatas and has attained the wisdom-mudrā of all eternal Tathāgatas, once again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called the Vajra Empowerment of the Wisdom-Mudrā of All Tathāgatas:
"The grasping of the body-mudrā of all Tathāgatas leads to the state of all Tathāgatas;
the grasping of the speech-mudrā leads to the attainment of all dharmas."
The adoption of the mind-seal (*cittamudrā*) conduces to the attainment of all meditative concentrations;
the adoption of the vajra-seal (*vajramudrā*) conduces to the supreme accomplishment of Vajrasattva of all body, speech, and mind—thus is *AṂ*.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is non-proliferated in all phenomena, again taught the method of the Perfection of Wisdom called the "Revolution of the Syllables of the Wheel."
All phenomena are empty by virtue of their lack of intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless by virtue of their signlessness;
all phenomena are wishless by virtue of the absence of aspiration.
"All phenomena are luminous by nature through the purity of the perfection of wisdom—AṂ.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is contained within the wheels of all Tathāgatas, again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "Entry into the Great Wheel":
"The entry into the equality of the vajra conduces to the entry into the wheel of the great bodhisattvas."
The entry into the equality of phenomena leads to the entry into the wheel of all phenomena; the entry into the equality of all things leads to the entry into all wheels—this is *raṃ*.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is the vessel for the full expansion of all methods of worship, again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Supreme of All Worship."

The generation of the thought of awakening is the extensive ritual for worshipping all Tathāgatas; the protection of the realm of all sentient beings is the extensive ritual for worshipping all Tathāgatas;
the upholding of the true Dharma is the extensive ritual for worshipping all Tathāgatas.
The extensive ritual for the worship of all Tathāgatas consists in the acts of writing, having written, upholding, reading, reciting, meditating upon, and worshipping the *Prajñāpāramitā*. Oṃ!

Then indeed, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvavinayasamartha, again taught this method of the *Prajñāpāramitā* called the "Womb of Wisdom for Subduing All Beings," which is the grasp of the Fist of Knowledge (*jñānamuṣṭiparigraha*).
Through the equality of all beings, there is the equality of wrath.
Through the disciplining of all sentient beings, there is the disciplining of anger;
through the dharmic nature of all sentient beings, there is the dharmic nature of anger;
through the vajra-nature of all sentient beings, there is the vajra-nature of anger.
For what reason? Because the training of all sentient beings is awakening (bodhi).
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata established in the equality of all phenomena, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Foremost of All Phenomena":
through the equality of all things, there is the equality of the perfection of wisdom.
The meaning of the perfection of wisdom is to be understood as the meaning of all things;
the nature of the perfection of wisdom is the nature of all phenomena;
and the activity of the perfection of wisdom is the activity of all actions. Hrīḥ.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Empowerment of All Sentient Beings":

"All sentient beings possess the embryo of the Tathāgata (*tathāgatagarbha*), because they have Samantabhadra, the Great Bodhisattva, as their universal self; all sentient beings are Vajragarbhas, because they have been consecrated as Vajragarbhas."
All sentient beings have the Dharma as their womb, by virtue of the setting forth of all speech;
all sentient beings have karma as their womb, by virtue of the application of the activities of all sentient beings. (TRĪ) *Note:
This passage, which is partially quoted in the *Sāramañjarī*, also survives in a Hoernle fragment, Or. 8672B(1); see Wille 2006b: 54. Note that Vairocana is absent!*

... this Prajñāpāramitā, named *Sarvasattvavinayajñānagarbha* (The Matrix of Knowledge for the Discipline of All Sentient Beings), which is free from the grasping of the fist of knowledge; it is the wrathful manifestation of the Perfection of Wisdom for the purpose of disciplining all sentient beings; [the wrathful manifestation] of the Perfection of Wisdom for the purpose of disciplining all sentient beings; the wrathful...
...of the nature of the *sattvavajra*; [of] the nature of the *krodhavajra*. For what reason?
...the Tathāgata is established in equanimity; furthermore...
[verso]

...the equality of all things is the equality of the perfection of wisdom; ...the nature of all things is the nature of the perfection of wisdom; through the state of all actions, the perfection of wisdom is ...
Furthermore, the Tathāgata again [taught] the perfection of wisdom called "The Empowerment of All Sentient Beings."
The Tathāgata-garbha, the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, by means of his entire self, is the Vajra.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who has reached the ultimate limit of the infinite and boundless, whose dharmas have reached the ultimate limit of the infinite and boundless, once again, for the sake of establishing the finality of this eon, taught this method of the Perfection of Wisdom called "The Vajra of the Establishment of the Finality of the Equality of All Dharmas":
"By the infinity of the Perfection of Wisdom, there is the infinity of all Tathāgatas."
Because the perfection of wisdom is limitless, all Tathāgatas are limitless;
because the perfection of wisdom is non-dual, all phenomena are non-dual;
because the perfection of wisdom is ultimately unestablished, all phenomena are ultimately unestablished—so it is said.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana—who has attained the secret nature of all Tathāgatas and is free from the conceptual proliferation of all phenomena—once again taught this entrance to the Prajñāpāramitā of the vajra-nature of the unfailing [teaching], called the Unfailing Vajra Samaya of Great Bliss. This supreme state, which is without beginning, end, or middle, leads to the supreme accomplishment of great passion for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of great bliss for the great Bodhisattvas;
and the supreme accomplishment of great bliss leads to the supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas for the great Bodhisattvas.

The supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas leads to the supreme accomplishment of the great Bodhisattvas in crushing all the great Māras. The supreme accomplishment of the great Bodhisattvas in crushing all the great Māras leads to the supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the entire great triple world. The supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the entire great triple world for the great Bodhisattvas leads to the supreme accomplishment of the ultimate, absolute great bliss—the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and the welfare and happiness of all sentient beings. SVĀṂ.
For what reason?
As long as these excellent sages remain here, established within existence,
so long are they able to perform incomparable benefit for sentient beings without passing into nirvāṇa.
Accomplished through the empowerment of the knowledge of the means and wisdom of the *prajñāpāramitā*, they become pure of existence for the sake of purifying all actions: HAṂ.
In this world, until the end of existence, those who discipline themselves through the subduing of passion and the like are always doers of evil; yet,
for the sake of purifying them, he himself has disciplined existence throughout all of existence until the end of existence.
Just as a deep red lotus is not stained by the defects of passion,
so those who work for the welfare of the world are never stained by the defects of worldly attachment.
"Purified by great passion, possessing great bliss and great wealth,
having attained sovereignty over the three realms, may they firmly accomplish that purpose. HĀ.
